It measures the number of employed persons and unemployed persons actively seeking work, as a percentage of the population of working age and indicates the potential work force for any group (See Figure II-12).
The third assumption is that the Crow population will have a net migration rate of zero; in other words in-migration will equal out-migration. The non-Crow population is expected to be highly mobile. Employment opportunities will determine the extent and timing of migration.
These assumptions appear to be reasonable for analytical purposes. However, it is recognized that Crow life-styles, including concepts and approaches to family size and patterns, as well as their propensity to migrate, may change drastically during the period under study.
The impact analysis has been done under two different assumptions about labor force participation behavior. The first assumption is referred to as the constant participation rate (LFPR-1) and assumes that labor force participation will continue at the rates derived from the 1970 Census. These rates provide a lower limit for the labor force that can be expected, given the size and characteristics of the area's population. The second assumption is referred to as the converging rate (LFPR-2), and assumes that the participation rates in the impact area will converge to projected rates by the year 1990 and that these rates will remain at that level through the year 2000.
